CCTV Policy

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how Alderbridge Care Group uses CCTV for the safety and security of people supported, staff and visitors. It applies to every site with installed CCTV, covering entrances and communal areas.

Policy statement

CCTV is used proportionately, for a specific, legitimate safety and security purpose, never as a general surveillance tool, and never in a location that would compromise personal dignity or privacy.

Definitions

**CCTV footage** recorded video from an installed camera. **Legitimate interest** the specific, documented safety and security purpose that provides the lawful basis for CCTV under the Data Protection Policy. **Retention period** the length of time footage is kept before automatic deletion, absent a specific reason to retain it longer.

Roles and responsibilities

**The registered manager or their deputy** is the only role authorised to view footage, and only for a specific, recorded purpose. **IT** maintains the technical system and retention settings. **The Data Protection Lead** advises on any request to view or disclose footage beyond routine internal review.

1. CCTV cameras are installed only at building entrances and communal areas, never in bedrooms, bathrooms, or other private areas.
2. Signage is displayed clearly wherever CCTV operates, informing anyone entering the area that recording is in progress.
3. Footage is retained for 31 days as standard, then automatically deleted, unless it is specifically retained longer because it relates to an ongoing incident, safeguarding concern, or legal matter.
4. Footage may only be viewed by the registered manager or their deputy, for a specific, recorded purpose such as investigating a reported incident.
5. Any request for footage from police or another external body is referred to the Data Protection Lead, who confirms the requester's legal basis before any disclosure.

Exceptions and professional judgement

Training and competency

Registered managers and deputies authorised to view footage complete data protection training covering the specific rules for CCTV.

Monitoring and compliance

The Data Protection Lead audits CCTV access logs periodically to confirm viewing has only occurred for a recorded, legitimate purpose.

Record keeping and retention

A log of every occasion footage is viewed, and why, is retained per the Records Retention Schedule, distinct from the footage itself.

Approval and review history

This policy was originally approved by the Chief Executive on 25 May 2025 and is scheduled for its next full review on 25 May 2026.

System maintenance and technical failure

Where a CCTV system develops a fault, IT logs and repairs it promptly, and the registered manager records the outage period, since a gap in CCTV coverage is itself a fact worth documenting in case it later becomes relevant to understanding what evidence is or is not available for a specific period.

Covert monitoring is not used

Alderbridge does not use covert or hidden cameras under any circumstance; every camera is visible and signposted, reflecting the principle that CCTV exists for a transparent, legitimate safety purpose rather than for surveillance staff or residents are not aware of.

Data subject rights relating to CCTV

A person appearing in CCTV footage may make a subject access request for that footage under the SAR Handling Procedure, with any other identifiable individual in the same footage redacted, following exactly the same redaction principles that procedure applies to any other record.

Installing a new camera or changing camera position

Any proposal to install a new camera or change an existing camera's field of view is reviewed by the Data Protection Lead before installation, confirming the proposed location still meets the entrances-and-communal-areas-only standard and updating the site's own signage accordingly, rather than a camera being added or repositioned informally by facilities staff without that documented review.

CCTV as evidence in a disciplinary or safeguarding process

Where footage is used as evidence in a disciplinary hearing or safeguarding investigation, it is handled and disclosed following the specific process each of those procedures already sets out, and access to it is limited to those directly involved in that specific process rather than more widely shared within the organisation, preserving both the integrity of the evidence and the privacy of everyone visible in it.

Reviewing whether additional CCTV coverage is genuinely justified

A request for additional CCTV coverage (for example, following a specific security concern) is assessed against this policy's proportionality principle before any new camera is installed, considering whether a less intrusive measure could achieve the same safety outcome, since CCTV expansion is treated as a genuine decision requiring justification, not a default response to any new concern that arises.

Communicating this policy to residents and families

New residents and their families are told about CCTV's presence and purpose as part of admission, in plain language rather than only through a general privacy notice, so that everyone entering an Alderbridge site understands clearly and early what is recorded, why, and how it is used, consistent with the transparency principle running through this policy as a whole.

Appendix: quick reference

For quick reference: strong unique passwords, never shared; lock your screen when you step away; no
unapproved software; no personal email or cloud storage for work data; report anything suspicious to IT
immediately; reasonable, limited personal use is fine.

Privileged and administrative accounts

Privileged IT accounts (for example, a system administrator account) are issued only to IT staff who
genuinely need them, reviewed every 6 months to confirm continued need, and never used for everyday
tasks like checking email, since routine use of a privileged account unnecessarily increases the damage a
compromised credential could cause.

Leaving Alderbridge: access removal

When an employee leaves, IT disables their system access on their last working day, coordinated with
HR's own leaver checklist, so that access does not linger unnecessarily after someone's employment
ends, and any shared account password they knew is changed as a routine precaution regardless of the
circumstances of their departure.

Using personal devices for approved purposes

Where a personal device is approved for a specific limited purpose (for example, the staff communication
app under the Mobile Device Management Policy), that approval does not extend to any other Alderbridge
system; a personal device is never used to access the care records system directly, regardless of how
convenient it might seem in the moment.

These guidance notes were originally approved by the Chief Executive on 6 April 2026 and are scheduled for their next full review on 6 April 2027.

Video calls and screen sharing while working remotely

During a video call or screen share involving sensitive information, staff confirm no unauthorised person can view or overhear the call, close any unrelated sensitive document before sharing a screen, and use only Alderbridge-approved conferencing tools rather than a personal account on an unapproved platform, applying the same care to a video meeting as to an in-person conversation about the same information.

Wi-Fi security at an approved home location

Home Wi-Fi used for Alderbridge work is secured with a strong, unique password and up-to-date router firmware, and an entirely open or default-password network is not used for any Alderbridge system; where genuinely uncertain about home network security, IT can advise on basic steps to improve it.

Ending a remote working arrangement

Where a remote working arrangement ends, whether by the employee's own request or a genuine business need, IT confirms the issued device and any remote access credential are returned or revoked promptly, following the same access-removal discipline the IT Acceptable Use Policy sets out for a leaver, since a remote arrangement ending is functionally similar to a change of access requirement even where employment itself continues.

Backing up work created while working remotely

Work saved locally on a remote device, rather than directly to an Alderbridge system, is backed up regularly using the approved method IT provides, since a device fault or loss while working remotely should never result in genuinely lost work, and staff are shown how to confirm their own backup is actually running correctly as part of their remote working setup.

Family members and household members during remote work

A family or household member should never have access to an Alderbridge device or account, even briefly and even for an unrelated purpose such as checking their own personal email, since this creates an unnecessary and entirely avoidable risk to data the household member has no reason to see.

Email Retention Policy

Supersedes the version effective 1 January 2025. Retention period shortened from 2 years to 6 months to

Retention

Mailboxes are retained for 6 months after an employee leaves (shortened from the previous 2-year
period), then permanently deleted.

Classification and filing

Email is a communication channel, not an indefinite records store. A message evidencing a care,
employment, contractual, complaint, safeguarding or governance decision is transferred promptly to the
approved record system and classified under the applicable retention schedule. Routine coordination,
duplicates, alerts and transient working messages are deleted when no longer needed.

Retention and disposal

Mailbox retention settings support, but do not replace, the duty to file a business record correctly.
Automatic deletion is suspended for a legal hold, investigation, subject-access search or other authorised
preservation requirement. When the hold ends, disposal resumes under the relevant schedule and is
recorded where the record class requires evidence of destruction.

Access and assurance

Managers arrange controlled mailbox access for absence, leavers or investigations through the
documented authorisation route; passwords are never shared. Information Governance reviews retention
configuration, preservation holds and exception reports at least annually. Staff report misdirected sensitive
email immediately under the Data Breach Procedure rather than attempting to resolve it silently.

Frequently asked questions

Key Safe Procedure

*Supersedes the Willow-Bank-only version effective 1 February 2025. Extended to cover the whole Midlands Region as community visiting expands to Oakfield Lodge's outreach service.*

Key safe codes

Community support workers across the Midlands Region (not only Willow Bank, as in the prior version) record each client's key safe code in the secure app, never on paper, and report any code change to the office within 24 hours.

Authorisation and coding

A key safe is installed only after property-owner consent, resident or representative agreement where applicable, and a recorded risk assessment. The code is disclosed only to authorised workers who need access and is not written in general notes, visit lists or an unprotected message. Each safe has a unique register entry linked to the address without exposing the code itself.

Use and security

Staff shield the keypad, return the key immediately, scramble the display and confirm the safe has locked before leaving. A missing key, damaged safe, observed code or unexplained access is reported immediately and the premises secured through the agreed contingency route. The code is changed after compromise and at other defined review points.

Review and removal

The responsible manager reviews continuing need, authorised recipients and physical condition at least annually and after a tenancy, care-package or risk change. When the safe is no longer required it is removed or disabled promptly, keys are returned and access records are closed. Installation, code-change, incident, review and removal evidence is retained securely.

Purpose and scope

These guidance notes set out how Central Support Office staff working under an agreed flexible arrangement keep Alderbridge data secure while working remotely. They apply to any employee approved to work away from an Alderbridge site.

Policy statement

Remote working is fully supported where a role allows it, provided the same data security standard applies regardless of location; working from home is never treated as a lower-security environment by default, but staff take specific, practical steps to make it genuinely as secure as an office setting.

Definitions

**Approved remote location** the employee's own home, or another location specifically agreed with their manager, as distinct from an unapproved public location. **Full-disk encryption** the device-level security control described in the Data Encryption Standard, required on any device used remotely. **VPN** a secure connection method used to access Alderbridge systems remotely where required.

Purpose and scope

Policy statement

IT systems at Alderbridge exist to support safe, high-quality care, not as a general convenience to be used
however an individual sees fit; this policy balances that operational purpose with a reasonable, trusted
allowance for ordinary personal use, and is enforced consistently rather than selectively.

Definitions

**Alderbridge system** any device, account, application or network Alderbridge owns, licenses or
otherwise provides for work use. **Acceptable use** use that is lawful, does not breach any other

limited, reasonable use of a work system for non-work purposes, permitted subject to the conditions in this
policy. **Privileged access** any account with elevated permissions beyond an ordinary user account,
such as an IT administrator account.

minor misuse concern informally in the first instance, escalating a serious concern to HR under the
Disciplinary Procedure.

Where a CCTV system develops a fault, IT logs and repairs it promptly, and the registered manager records the outage period, since a gap in CCTV coverage is itself a fact worth documenting in case it later becomes relevant to understanding what evidence is or is not available for a specific period.

Covert monitoring is not used

Alderbridge does not use covert or hidden cameras under any circumstance; every camera is visible and signposted, reflecting the principle that CCTV exists for a transparent, legitimate safety purpose rather than for surveillance staff or residents are not aware of.

Data subject rights relating to CCTV

A person appearing in CCTV footage may make a subject access request for that footage under the SAR Handling Procedure, with any other identifiable individual in the same footage redacted, following exactly the same redaction principles that procedure applies to any other record.

Installing a new camera or changing camera position

Any proposal to install a new camera or change an existing camera's field of view is reviewed by the Data Protection Lead before installation, confirming the proposed location still meets the entrances-and-communal-areas-only standard and updating the site's own signage accordingly, rather than a camera being added or repositioned informally by facilities staff without that documented review.

CCTV as evidence in a disciplinary or safeguarding process

Where footage is used as evidence in a disciplinary hearing or safeguarding investigation, it is handled and disclosed following the specific process each of those procedures already sets out, and access to it is limited to those directly involved in that specific process rather than more widely shared within the organisation, preserving both the integrity of the evidence and the privacy of everyone visible in it.

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how Alderbridge Care Group uses CCTV for the safety and security of people supported, staff and visitors. It applies to every site with installed CCTV, covering entrances and communal areas.

Policy statement

CCTV is used proportionately, for a specific, legitimate safety and security purpose, never as a general surveillance tool, and never in a location that would compromise personal dignity or privacy.

Definitions

**CCTV footage** recorded video from an installed camera. **Legitimate interest** the specific, documented safety and security purpose that provides the lawful basis for CCTV under the Data Protection Policy. **Retention period** the length of time footage is kept before automatic deletion, absent a specific reason to retain it longer.

Roles and responsibilities

**The registered manager or their deputy** is the only role authorised to view footage, and only for a specific, recorded purpose. **IT** maintains the technical system and retention settings. **The Data Protection Lead** advises on any request to view or disclose footage beyond routine internal review.

1. CCTV cameras are installed only at building entrances and communal areas, never in bedrooms, bathrooms, or other private areas.
2. Signage is displayed clearly wherever CCTV operates, informing anyone entering the area that recording is in progress.
3. Footage is retained for 31 days as standard, then automatically deleted, unless it is specifically retained longer because it relates to an ongoing incident, safeguarding concern, or legal matter.
4. Footage may only be viewed by the registered manager or their deputy, for a specific, recorded purpose such as investigating a reported incident.
5. Any request for footage from police or another external body is referred to the Data Protection Lead, who confirms the requester's legal basis before any disclosure.

Extended worked example: a reasonable adjustment for a resident

A worked example illustrates that this policy's dignity commitment applies to people supported, not only staff. A resident at Riverside House living with a visual impairment finds it increasingly difficult to identify her own room among several similar doors on her corridor. maximum possible time within that window to investigate properly and, where required, notify the ICO with
a genuinely complete, accurate assessment rather than a rushed, incomplete one submitted only to beat
the deadline.

Breaches involving a third-party data processor

Where a breach occurs at a third-party data processor holding Alderbridge data (for example, a payroll
provider), the processor's own contractual obligation to notify Alderbridge without undue delay is relied on,
but the Data Protection Lead also proactively checks in with key processors periodically, since the 72-hour
clock for Alderbridge's own notification obligation still runs from when Alderbridge itself becomes aware,
which can be later than when the processor's own breach actually occurred if the processor is slow to tell
Alderbridge.

Extended frequently asked questions

**What if the breach involves a former employee's data rather than a current one?** The same procedure
applies in full; a former employee's data remains protected personal data for as long as Alderbridge holds
it. **Can a breach be assessed as low risk simply because the recipient is another Alderbridge employee
rather than an external party?** No — an internal misdirection can still be a genuine breach, particularly for
special category health data, and is assessed on the actual risk to the individual concerned, not assumed
low risk purely because it stayed within the organisation. **Is a physical break-in and theft of paper records
treated the same as a digital breach?** Yes — the same assessment and notification process applies
regardless of whether the compromised data was digital or physical.

Assurance and records

The registered manager reviews the log monthly for missed checks and repeated marginal readings. The facilities lead reviews contractor reports, corrective actions and trend data quarterly. Key Cutting and Access Card Procedure

Supersedes the version effective 1 March 2025. Adds a new access-card return clause on leaving; removes the prior 4-week waiting period.

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how a site key or access card is issued to, and returned by, a staff member. It applies to every permanent member of staff.

Policy statement

Site keys or access cards are issued to permanent staff from their first day, the previous 4-week waiting period having been removed, logged in the key register, and every key and access card must now be returned on an employee's last working day.

Definitions

**Key register** the log recording every key or access card issued, to whom, and when, and now its confirmed return date. **First-day issue** the new standard replacing the previous 4-week qualifying period. **Leaver return** the new requirement that every key and access card is returned before final pay is released.

Roles and responsibilities

**The registered manager** authorises a key or access card issue from a staff member's first day, and confirms return on their last working day before final pay is released. **Facilities** cuts a key or programs an access card and updates the key register, now including the return date. **The staff member** keeps their key or access card secure, reports a lost one immediately, and returns it on their last working day.

Issue a key or access card to a permanent staff member from their first day; the previous 4-week qualifying period has been removed.

Log every key or access card issued in the key register, including the recipient and issue date.

Report a lost key or access card to Facilities immediately, who assesses whether a lock or access code change is needed.

Return all keys and access cards to the registered manager on an employee's last working day, before their final pay is released; this is a new requirement introduced in this version.

The individual moving and handling risk assessment in detail

Every MHRA records, at minimum, the person's current weight-bearing ability, their level of cooperation and understanding of what is being asked of them, the specific equipment required (including sling size and hoist type where relevant), the number of staff required, any specific technique variation (for example, a preferred side to approach from following a stroke), and the date of the last review; a care worker unfamiliar with a person for the first time (for example, covering an unfamiliar shift) is expected to read the full MHRA before providing any assistance, not only a summary or a colleague's verbal description of what is normally done.

When an MHRA needs an urgent, unscheduled review

An MHRA is reviewed immediately, not at the next routine 6-month point, following any fall, any hospital admission, any surgery, or any other event that could plausibly have changed a person's mobility, strength, or cooperation; the registered manager is responsible for identifying when such a trigger has occurred and ensuring the review happens before the person is next assisted to move, even where this means a temporary, more cautious default technique is used in the interim while the full review is arranged.

Bariatric and specialist equipment needs

Where a person's weight or body shape means standard equipment is not suitable, a specialist bariatric assessment is arranged, specifying bariatric-rated hoists, slings and, where needed, wider doorways or reinforced flooring; this assessment is treated with particular care and dignity, discussed sensitively with the person and their family, and reviewed by the Health and Safety Lead directly rather than left solely to the site's own moving and handling champion given the additional equipment and structural considerations involved.

A community support worker arrives at a scheduled visit and finds an unfamiliar, agitated visitor already at the property who was not expected. Rather than proceeding with the visit as planned, the worker withdraws immediately, calls the office from a safe distance, and the office arranges a police welfare check on the client before any further visit is attempted; the incident is logged, the address is flagged for a two-person visit going forward until the situation is better understood, and the worker's decision to withdraw is explicitly praised at the next team meeting as exactly the response this policy expects, not questioned for having left before completing the scheduled care task.

CCTV Policy

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how Alderbridge Care Group uses CCTV for the safety and security of people supported, staff and visitors. It applies to every site with installed CCTV, covering entrances and communal areas.

Policy statement

CCTV is used proportionately, for a specific, legitimate safety and security purpose, never as a general surveillance tool, and never in a location that would compromise personal dignity or privacy.

Definitions

**CCTV footage** recorded video from an installed camera. **Legitimate interest** the specific, documented safety and security purpose that provides the lawful basis for CCTV under the Data Protection Policy. **Retention period** the length of time footage is kept before automatic deletion, absent a specific reason to retain it longer.

Roles and responsibilities

**The registered manager or their deputy** is the only role authorised to view footage, and only for a specific, recorded purpose. **IT** maintains the technical system and retention settings. **The Data Protection Lead** advises on any request to view or disclose footage beyond routine internal review.

1. CCTV cameras are installed only at building entrances and communal areas, never in bedrooms, bathrooms, or other private areas.

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how Alderbridge Care Group uses CCTV for the safety and security of people supported, staff and visitors. It applies to every site with installed CCTV, covering entrances and communal areas.

Policy statement

CCTV is used proportionately, for a specific, legitimate safety and security purpose, never as a general surveillance tool, and never in a location that would compromise personal dignity or privacy.

Definitions

**CCTV footage** recorded video from an installed camera. **Legitimate interest** the specific, documented safety and security purpose that provides the lawful basis for CCTV under the Data Protection Policy. **Retention period** the length of time footage is kept before automatic deletion, absent a specific reason to retain it longer.

Roles and responsibilities

**The registered manager or their deputy** is the only role authorised to view footage, and only for a specific, recorded purpose. **IT** maintains the technical system and retention settings. **The Data Protection Lead** advises on any request to view or disclose footage beyond routine internal review.

1. CCTV cameras are installed only at building entrances and communal areas, never in bedrooms, bathrooms, or other private areas.
2. Signage is displayed clearly wherever CCTV operates, informing anyone entering the area that recording is in progress.
3. Footage is retained for 31 days as standard, then automatically deleted, unless it is specifically retained longer because it relates to an ongoing incident, safeguarding concern, or legal matter.
4. Footage may only be viewed by the registered manager or their deputy, for a specific, recorded purpose such as investigating a reported incident.
5. Any request for footage from police or another external body is referred to the Data Protection Lead, who confirms the requester's legal basis before any disclosure.

Exceptions and professional judgement

4. Footage may only be viewed by the registered manager or their deputy, for a specific, recorded purpose such as investigating a reported incident.
5. Any request for footage from police or another external body is referred to the Data Protection Lead, who confirms the requester's legal basis before any disclosure.

Exceptions and professional judgement

Where footage might be relevant to a safeguarding investigation not yet formally opened, the registered manager may view it on a precautionary basis, recording the reason, provided this remains within the narrow, documented purpose CCTV is installed for rather than becoming a general investigative tool.

Local and regional variations

CCTV camera placement varies by site reflecting each building's own layout, but the underlying rules — entrances and communal areas only, never private areas — apply identically everywhere.

Training and competency

Monitoring and compliance

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how Alderbridge Care Group uses CCTV for the safety and security of people supported, staff and visitors. It applies to every site with installed CCTV, covering entrances and communal areas.

Policy statement

CCTV is used proportionately, for a specific, legitimate safety and security purpose, never as a general surveillance tool, and never in a location that would compromise personal dignity or privacy.

Definitions

**CCTV footage** recorded video from an installed camera. **Legitimate interest** the specific, documented safety and security purpose that provides the lawful basis for CCTV under the Data Protection Policy. **Retention period** the length of time footage is kept before automatic deletion, absent a specific reason to retain it longer.

Roles and responsibilities

**The registered manager or their deputy** is the only role authorised to view footage, and only for a specific, recorded purpose. **IT** maintains the technical system and retention settings. **The Data Protection Lead** advises on any request to view or disclose footage beyond routine internal review.

1. CCTV cameras are installed only at building entrances and communal areas, never in bedrooms, bathrooms, or other private areas.
2. Signage is displayed clearly wherever CCTV operates, informing anyone entering the area that recording is in progress.
3. Footage is retained for 31 days as standard, then automatically deleted, unless it is specifically retained longer because it relates to an ongoing incident, safeguarding concern, or legal matter.

Key safe codes

Community support workers across the Midlands Region (not only Willow Bank, as in the prior version) record each client's key safe code in the secure app, never on paper, and report any code change to the office within 24 hours.

Authorisation and coding

A key safe is installed only after property-owner consent, resident or representative agreement where applicable, and a recorded risk assessment. Use and security

Staff shield the keypad, return the key immediately, scramble the display and confirm the safe has locked before leaving. Review and removal

The responsible manager reviews continuing need, authorised recipients and physical condition at least annually and after a tenancy, care-package or risk change. Appendix: examples that would and would not typically qualify

For illustration only. Would typically qualify: a genuine, reasonably held concern about unsafe staffing,
financial irregularity, a cover-up of a safeguarding incident, or a health and safety risk being deliberately
ignored. Would not typically qualify as a protected disclosure, though may still be a legitimate grievance: a
personal dispute about your own pay or duties with no wider public interest element, or a concern raised
purely to settle a personal grievance against a named individual with no genuine underlying malpractice
concern. Where it is genuinely unclear which category a concern falls into, it is treated as a protected
disclosure under this policy by default, since the cost of investigating a concern that turns out to be an
ordinary grievance is far lower than the cost of failing to protect someone who has genuinely raised a

International data transfers

Alderbridge's default position is that personal data about people supported and staff is held within the UK
or European Economic Area. Any proposed arrangement that would transfer personal data outside that
area is referred to the Data Protection Lead before it proceeds, so that an appropriate safeguard — for

assumed to be acceptable merely because a supplier is otherwise reputable or because the transfer is

Extended worked example: a subject access request from a family
member

A worked example illustrates a common point of confusion. A family member of a resident at Harbour View
asks reception for a copy of 'all the notes about my mother.' Reception does not simply print the requested
notes. Instead, the request is passed to the Data Protection Lead the same day, who first confirms
whether the family member holds a valid authority (for example, a registered Lasting Power of Attorney for
health and welfare, or the resident's own explicit consent) to receive their mother's personal data at all — a
family relationship alone does not automatically confer that right, even where the family member is a
regular, trusted visitor. Where valid authority exists, the request is then handled as a genuine subject
access request under the Subject Access Request Handling Procedure's own one-month timescale, with
any information about another person (for example, a note referring to another resident) redacted before
disclosure. Where no valid authority exists, the Data Protection Lead explains this sensitively to the family
member and discusses what, if any, more limited information can still appropriately be shared directly with
them as part of ordinary care communication rather than under the formal subject access process.

Worked example

Protection Lead** confirms the requester's identity and any authority claimed, coordinates gathering the relevant records across every system that might hold them, and completes any necessary redaction before disclosure. **Each registered manager and HR** supports the Data Protection Lead by identifying and providing the records held at their own site or function promptly when asked.

Confirm the request is genuinely a SAR (a request to see personal data), rather than a different kind of enquiry that might be better handled another way, though where genuinely unclear, treat it as a SAR by default.

Confirm the requester's identity and, where they are not the data subject themselves, their valid authority to receive the data subject's personal data.

Search every relevant system and paper record for personal data about the requester, not only the most obvious source (for example, the care record alone, when email correspondence might also be relevant).

Review every document found and redact any third-party personal data it contains, unless that third party has consented to its disclosure.

Prepare a response explaining what personal data is held, why it is processed, who it is shared with, and how long it is retained, alongside the actual data itself.

Respond within one calendar month of receipt, or explain in writing before that deadline why a genuinely complex request needs the further two-month extension this procedure allows, rather than simply missing the deadline without explanation.

Record the request and its outcome, including the time taken, so response-time compliance can be monitored across every SAR received.

Exceptions and professional judgement

Where disclosing specific information would cause serious harm to the data subject's own physical or mental health (a narrow exemption available for health data specifically), the Data Protection Lead seeks a clinical opinion before deciding whether to withhold that specific element, and any such withholding is explained to the requester as far as possible without disclosing the harmful information itself, rather than used as a general excuse to withhold inconvenient information.

IT and Communications Acceptable Use Policy

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how staff use Alderbridge Care Group's IT and communications systems responsibly
and securely. It applies to every device, account and system Alderbridge provides or permits access
through, and to every employee, agency worker, contractor and volunteer with any level of access.

Policy statement

IT systems at Alderbridge exist to support safe, high-quality care, not as a general convenience to be used
however an individual sees fit; this policy balances that operational purpose with a reasonable, trusted
allowance for ordinary personal use, and is enforced consistently rather than selectively.

Definitions

**Alderbridge system** any device, account, application or network Alderbridge owns, licenses or
otherwise provides for work use. **Acceptable use** use that is lawful, does not breach any other
Alderbridge policy, and does not create an unreasonable security or reputational risk. **Personal use**
limited, reasonable use of a work system for non-work purposes, permitted subject to the conditions in this
policy. **Privileged access** any account with elevated permissions beyond an ordinary user account,
such as an IT administrator account.

Roles and responsibilities

**Every member of staff** uses Alderbridge systems in line with this policy and reports any suspected
security concern to the IT service desk immediately. **IT** maintains technical controls (password policy,
antivirus, monitoring) and investigates any reported or detected concern. **Line managers** address a
minor misuse concern informally in the first instance, escalating a serious concern to HR under the
Disciplinary Procedure.

1. Use a strong, unique password for every Alderbridge account, at least 12 characters, never shared with
another person including a colleague covering your shift.

2. Lock your screen whenever you step away from a device that can access care records or other
sensitive information.

CCTV Policy

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how Alderbridge Care Group uses CCTV for the safety and security of people supported, staff and visitors. It applies to every site with installed CCTV, covering entrances and communal areas.

Policy statement

CCTV is used proportionately, for a specific, legitimate safety and security purpose, never as a general surveillance tool, and never in a location that would compromise personal dignity or privacy.

Definitions

**CCTV footage** recorded video from an installed camera. **Legitimate interest** the specific, documented safety and security purpose that provides the lawful basis for CCTV under the Data Protection Policy. **Retention period** the length of time footage is kept before automatic deletion, absent a specific reason to retain it longer.

Roles and responsibilities

**The registered manager or their deputy** is the only role authorised to view footage, and only for a specific, recorded purpose. **IT** maintains the technical system and retention settings. **The Data Protection Lead** advises on any request to view or disclose footage beyond routine internal review.

1. CCTV cameras are installed only at building entrances and communal areas, never in bedrooms, bathrooms, or other private areas.
2. Signage is displayed clearly wherever CCTV operates, informing anyone entering the area that recording is in progress.
3. Footage is retained for 31 days as standard, then automatically deleted, unless it is specifically retained longer because it relates to an ongoing incident, safeguarding concern, or legal matter.
4. Footage may only be viewed by the registered manager or their deputy, for a specific, recorded purpose such as investigating a reported incident.
5. Any request for footage from police or another external body is referred to the Data Protection Lead, who confirms the requester's legal basis before any disclosure.

Exceptions and professional judgement

Missing Person Procedure

Supersedes the version effective 1 July 2024. Immediate-search window shortened from 30 to 15 minutes.

1. Immediate search

A 15-minute site and immediate-grounds search is conducted (shortened from the previous 30 minutes)
before escalating further.

2. Police contact

If not found after the immediate search, police are called on 101 (or 999 if there is immediate risk).

Immediate response

Staff confirm the person is not elsewhere on site, note the last verified sighting, clothing, mobility,
communication needs and likely destinations, and preserve relevant CCTV or access records. The
registered manager assesses immediate vulnerability and calls emergency services without delay where
risk is high; local searching never postpones a necessary police report.

Search and communication

The search is coordinated, logged and allocated so unsafe duplication and unsearched areas are visible.
Staff maintain safe staffing for residents who remain on site. Family, commissioners and safeguarding
contacts are informed according to the person's plan and the circumstances, while public communication
and photographs are released only through the police-led or otherwise authorised route.

Return and learning

On return, immediate welfare and medical needs are assessed before a calm account is sought. The care
plan, risk assessment and known triggers are reviewed with the person and relevant representatives. The
incident record includes timings, decisions, notifications and search activity, and repeated episodes or
control failures are escalated for safeguarding and service-level review.

Email Retention Policy

Retention

Classification and filing

Local and regional variations

No local or regional variation applies to this procedure — disciplinary process is deliberately standardised across all five sites and Central Support Office to ensure consistent, fair treatment regardless of location.

Monitoring and compliance

HR reviews disciplinary outcomes quarterly across all sites for consistency, looking specifically for any pattern suggesting a particular site or manager is applying the process more or less severely than others.

Record keeping and retention

Disciplinary records are retained for 6 years after employment ends, in line with the Records Retention Schedule, and a warning that has expired is disregarded for any future decision even though the record itself is retained for reference.

Frequently asked questions

**Can I bring a friend from outside work to the hearing?** No — the right to be accompanied is limited to a trade union representative or a work colleague, not a friend or family member from outside Alderbridge. **Does a final written warning mean my next mistake results in dismissal automatically?** No — dismissal is never automatic; a further formal hearing is still held, considering the specific circumstances, though a further offence while a final warning is live makes dismissal a realistic outcome.

Approval and review history

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

This procedure works alongside, and does not replace, the Grievance Procedure, the Safeguarding Adults Policy, the Allegations Against Staff Procedure, and the Probationary Period Policy. Where the concern is a probationary employee's conduct, HR advises on whether the shortened probationary process or this full procedure is more appropriate given the seriousness of the matter; where the matter also raises a safeguarding concern, the Safeguarding Adults Policy and Allegations Against Staff Procedure run in parallel, as described in that policy's own cross-reference to this one.

Approval and review history

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

Extended worked example: a reasonable adjustment for a resident

A worked example illustrates that this policy's dignity commitment applies to people supported, not only staff. A resident at Riverside House living with a visual impairment finds it increasingly difficult to identify her own room among several similar doors on her corridor. Rather than treating this as an inevitable consequence of her condition, staff introduce a simple, high-contrast tactile marker on her door, chosen together with her rather than imposed, and the change is recorded in her care plan as a reasonable adjustment. The registered manager subsequently reviews whether other residents on the same corridor might benefit from a similar approach, rather than treating the adjustment as a one-off fix specific to a single request.

Record keeping and retention

MAR charts, controlled drugs registers and medication error reports are retained for 8 years in line with the Records Retention Schedule, aligned with the wider care-record retention period rather than treated as a shorter-lived operational record.

Frequently asked questions

**What if a resident is asleep at the scheduled time?** A reasonable, brief delay is acceptable and should be recorded as a timing variance rather than an omission, provided the medication is still given within the time-critical window the prescriber has specified where one applies. **Can a family member give medication during a visit?** No — medication administration remains a staff responsibility at all times, even during a family visit, unless a specific self-administration arrangement is separately authorised under the Self-Administration of Medication Policy. **What happens if the pharmacy sends the wrong strength?** The delivery is not placed into stock; it is quarantined, the pharmacy is contacted the same day, and the previous supply continues to be used if sufficient stock remains.

Appendix: common substances and their key controls

For quick reference: general-purpose cleaning products typically require gloves only; strong descalers and

Successful completion of probation is confirmed to the employee in writing, normally by the end of the 6-month period.

Where performance or conduct concerns cannot be resolved, employment may be ended with the applicable statutory or contractual notice, whichever is greater, without the full Disciplinary Procedure applying during probation.

Exceptions and professional judgement

Where a probationary employee's absence pattern reaches a Sickness Absence Policy trigger point, the line manager and HR consider the specific circumstances (for example, a short-term illness clearly unrelated to any underlying concern) before deciding whether this affects the probation outcome, rather than applying a mechanical rule regardless of context.

Local and regional variations

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

Worked example

A worked example illustrates an extension used constructively. A new care worker at Moorland View shows promise but has not yet completed all mandatory training by the 5-month review due to a training provider's own scheduling delay, through no fault of the employee. The registered manager extends probation by 6 weeks specifically to allow the outstanding training to be completed and properly assessed, rather than making a premature decision based on an incomplete picture.

Frequently asked questions

**Can probation be confirmed early, before 6 months?** Yes, where a manager is confident the standard has clearly been met, probation may be confirmed early with HR's agreement. **What support is available if I'm struggling during probation?** Raise it with your line manager as early as possible; additional supervised practice, a revised learning plan, or occupational health referral are all considered depending on the nature of the difficulty. **Does a probationary employee have the same rights as a confirmed employee?** Yes to the same core employment rights, though the process for ending employment during probation is simpler, as this policy describes.

Tracking

Appendix: the 72-hour clock at a glance

For quick reference: the clock starts when Alderbridge becomes aware of the breach, not when the
investigation concludes; internal reporting within 1 hour of discovery gives the Data Protection Lead the
maximum possible time within that window to investigate properly and, where required, notify the ICO with
a genuinely complete, accurate assessment rather than a rushed, incomplete one submitted only to beat
the deadline.

Breaches involving a third-party data processor

Where a breach occurs at a third-party data processor holding Alderbridge data (for example, a payroll
provider), the processor's own contractual obligation to notify Alderbridge without undue delay is relied on,
but the Data Protection Lead also proactively checks in with key processors periodically, since the 72-hour
clock for Alderbridge's own notification obligation still runs from when Alderbridge itself becomes aware,
which can be later than when the processor's own breach actually occurred if the processor is slow to tell
Alderbridge.

Extended frequently asked questions

**What if the breach involves a former employee's data rather than a current one?** The same procedure
applies in full; a former employee's data remains protected personal data for as long as Alderbridge holds
it. **Can a breach be assessed as low risk simply because the recipient is another Alderbridge employee
rather than an external party?** No — an internal misdirection can still be a genuine breach, particularly for
special category health data, and is assessed on the actual risk to the individual concerned, not assumed
low risk purely because it stayed within the organisation. **Is a physical break-in and theft of paper records
treated the same as a digital breach?** Yes — the same assessment and notification process applies
regardless of whether the compromised data was digital or physical.

Legionella Control Procedure

*Supersedes the version effective 1 March 2025. Sections reordered for readability; no requirement changed.*

Responsibility

The Facilities Lead maintains the legionella risk assessment and monitoring log for every site.

Water temperature monitoring

Hot water outlets are checked monthly to confirm they reach 50°C within one minute at the tap. Cold water outlets are checked to confirm they remain below 20°C.

Flushing of little-used outlets

Any outlet unused for more than a week is flushed for at least 2 minutes to prevent stagnation.

Control programme

The responsible person maintains a written scheme covering hot and cold-water temperatures, sentinel outlets, little-used outlets, shower-head cleaning and the response to an out-of-range result. Maintenance staff record each check against the asset and outlet identifier so a missed check can be distinguished from a compliant reading. A room closure, plumbing alteration or prolonged vacancy triggers a fresh assessment before the outlet returns to use.

Out-of-range response

A temperature or hygiene result outside the written scheme is reported to the registered manager and facilities lead on the same working day. The outlet is isolated where continued use could expose a resident or staff member, remedial flushing or engineering work is commissioned, and reopening requires a documented satisfactory recheck. A suspected case of legionellosis is escalated immediately through infection-control and public-health routes rather than managed as routine maintenance.

Assurance and records

The registered manager reviews the log monthly for missed checks and repeated marginal readings. The facilities lead reviews contractor reports, corrective actions and trend data quarterly. Risk assessments, schematics, monitoring records, laboratory results and remedial-work evidence are retained together so an auditor can reconstruct the control history for each water system.

Key Cutting and Access Card Procedure

Supersedes the version effective 1 March 2025. Adds a new access-card return clause on leaving; removes the prior 4-week waiting period.

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how a site key or access card is issued to, and returned by, a staff member. It applies to every permanent member of staff.

Policy statement

Site keys or access cards are issued to permanent staff from their first day, the previous 4-week waiting period having been removed, logged in the key register, and every key and access card must now be returned on an employee's last working day.

Definitions

**Key register** the log recording every key or access card issued, to whom, and when, and now its confirmed return date. **First-day issue** the new standard replacing the previous 4-week qualifying period. **Leaver return** the new requirement that every key and access card is returned before final pay is released.

Roles and responsibilities

**The registered manager** authorises a key or access card issue from a staff member's first day, and confirms return on their last working day before final pay is released. **Facilities** cuts a key or programs an access card and updates the key register, now including the return date. **The staff member** keeps their key or access card secure, reports a lost one immediately, and returns it on their last working day.

Log every key or access card issued in the key register, including the recipient and issue date.

Report a lost key or access card to Facilities immediately, who assesses whether a lock or access code change is needed.

The individual moving and handling risk assessment in detail

Every MHRA records, at minimum, the person's current weight-bearing ability, their level of cooperation and understanding of what is being asked of them, the specific equipment required (including sling size and hoist type where relevant), the number of staff required, any specific technique variation (for example, a preferred side to approach from following a stroke), and the date of the last review; a care worker unfamiliar with a person for the first time (for example, covering an unfamiliar shift) is expected to read the full MHRA before providing any assistance, not only a summary or a colleague's verbal description of what is normally done.

When an MHRA needs an urgent, unscheduled review

An MHRA is reviewed immediately, not at the next routine 6-month point, following any fall, any hospital admission, any surgery, or any other event that could plausibly have changed a person's mobility, strength, or cooperation; the registered manager is responsible for identifying when such a trigger has occurred and ensuring the review happens before the person is next assisted to move, even where this means a temporary, more cautious default technique is used in the interim while the full review is arranged.

Bariatric and specialist equipment needs

A community support worker arrives at a scheduled visit and finds an unfamiliar, agitated visitor already at the property who was not expected. CCTV Policy

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how Alderbridge Care Group uses CCTV for the safety and security of people supported, staff and visitors. It applies to every site with installed CCTV, covering entrances and communal areas.

Policy statement

CCTV is used proportionately, for a specific, legitimate safety and security purpose, never as a general surveillance tool, and never in a location that would compromise personal dignity or privacy.

Definitions

**CCTV footage** recorded video from an installed camera. **Legitimate interest** the specific, documented safety and security purpose that provides the lawful basis for CCTV under the Data Protection Policy. **Retention period** the length of time footage is kept before automatic deletion, absent a specific reason to retain it longer.

Roles and responsibilities

**The registered manager or their deputy** is the only role authorised to view footage, and only for a specific, recorded purpose. **IT** maintains the technical system and retention settings. **The Data Protection Lead** advises on any request to view or disclose footage beyond routine internal review.

1. CCTV cameras are installed only at building entrances and communal areas, never in bedrooms, bathrooms, or other private areas.
2. Signage is displayed clearly wherever CCTV operates, informing anyone entering the area that recording is in progress.
3. Footage is retained for 31 days as standard, then automatically deleted, unless it is specifically retained longer because it relates to an ongoing incident, safeguarding concern, or legal matter.
4. Footage may only be viewed by the registered manager or their deputy, for a specific, recorded purpose such as investigating a reported incident.
5. Any request for footage from police or another external body is referred to the Data Protection Lead, who confirms the requester's legal basis before any disclosure.

Exceptions and professional judgement

Reviewing whether additional CCTV coverage is genuinely justified

A request for additional CCTV coverage (for example, following a specific security concern) is assessed against this policy's proportionality principle before any new camera is installed, considering whether a less intrusive measure could achieve the same safety outcome, since CCTV expansion is treated as a genuine decision requiring justification, not a default response to any new concern that arises.

Communicating this policy to residents and families

New residents and their families are told about CCTV's presence and purpose as part of admission, in plain language rather than only through a general privacy notice, so that everyone entering an Alderbridge site understands clearly and early what is recorded, why, and how it is used, consistent with the transparency principle running through this policy as a whole.

Where a CCTV system develops a fault, IT logs and repairs it promptly, and the registered manager records the outage period, since a gap in CCTV coverage is itself a fact worth documenting in case it later becomes relevant to understanding what evidence is or is not available for a specific period.

Covert monitoring is not used

Alderbridge does not use covert or hidden cameras under any circumstance; every camera is visible and signposted, reflecting the principle that CCTV exists for a transparent, legitimate safety purpose rather than for surveillance staff or residents are not aware of.

Data subject rights relating to CCTV

A person appearing in CCTV footage may make a subject access request for that footage under the SAR Handling Procedure, with any other identifiable individual in the same footage redacted, following exactly the same redaction principles that procedure applies to any other record.

Installing a new camera or changing camera position

Any proposal to install a new camera or change an existing camera's field of view is reviewed by the Data Protection Lead before installation, confirming the proposed location still meets the entrances-and-communal-areas-only standard and updating the site's own signage accordingly, rather than a camera being added or repositioned informally by facilities staff without that documented review.

CCTV as evidence in a disciplinary or safeguarding process

Where footage is used as evidence in a disciplinary hearing or safeguarding investigation, it is handled and disclosed following the specific process each of those procedures already sets out, and access to it is limited to those directly involved in that specific process rather than more widely shared within the organisation, preserving both the integrity of the evidence and the privacy of everyone visible in it.
